$comment: The reverse index into docs/layers.json: from a library a project already
depends on, to the kiwa layer that tests it.
docs/layers.json answers 'what does this layer need'. This file answers the
question `kiwa init --detect` actually asks, which is the other way round:
here is a Cargo.toml, which layers apply.
Two kinds of entry, and they are not interchangeable:
generated  Six packages name their target libraries in peerDependencies
(auth, orm, cache, queue, ui, dapp). Those lists are the
declaration; scripts/rebuild-stack-signals.mjs copies them here
and --check fails when a peer is added without regenerating.
manual     The rest declare only `vitest` or nothing at all — nextjs, edge,
hono, fresh, solidjs, and the ai-realtime four plus component.
Their adapters mock the framework rather than importing it, so
there is nothing to read. Eleven packages, written by hand.
The boundary is not arbitrary: it lines up with the categories in
docs/libraries.json. Services are transparent, frameworks and ai-realtime are
opaque.
Precedence. A signal can point at more than one layer — `ioredis` serves both
cache and job-queue, `axum` appears in a project whose real subject is
tower-http. `strength` orders them: an `exact` signal settles the question, a
`weak` one only applies when no exact signal claimed the same layer group.
For Rust the exact signal is the kiwa-test-rs feature, because the framework
dependency alone cannot tell rust-axum from rust-tower-http — the tower-http
example depends on axum too.
This file only lists what a manifest can show. Detection never installs;
`kiwa init --detect` prints and writes .kiwa/stack.json, and `--apply` is a
separate step. A wrong guess costs a line of output.

`also` exists because one dependency can imply more than one layer. The adapter package serves the unit and the integration layer alike, and nothing in Cargo.toml or go.mod distinguishes them: rust-cargo-poc has tests/poc.rs and tests/poc_integration.rs and one kiwa-test-rs entry. Reporting only the unit layer would hide half of what the project already tests.

rust.note: Presence of the adapter means both the unit and the integration layer. A manifest cannot tell them apart — rust-cargo-poc carries tests/poc.rs and tests/poc_integration.rs against the same dependency — so both are reported and the caller narrows it.
rust-tower-http-poc depends on axum as well, so this only applies when no feature said otherwise.

go.note: Presence of the adapter means both the unit and the integration layer. A manifest cannot tell them apart — rust-cargo-poc carries tests/poc.rs and tests/poc_integration.rs against the same dependency — so both are reported and the caller narrows it.
